root_cause.text: The mac80211 `ieee80211_parse_adv_t2l` function unconditionally reads a link map presence indicator byte from a TTLM element, even when the element uses a default link map (indicated by the control field), causing an out-of-bounds read one byte beyond the element’s end.
root_cause.evidence: The patch conditionally adds `if (!(control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP))` before reading `link_map_presence` and advancing `pos`, and the CVE description states that TTLM elements with a default mapping do not contain a presence indicator, and mac80211 "would incorrectly parse the frame and would also read one byte beyond the end of the element."

vuln_statements.explanation: Defines the variable link_map_presence which will hold the unconditionally read byte; the out-of-bounds read occurs when this variable is assigned without checking if the link map is default.
Pointer used to traverse the element data; the out-of-bounds read happens when pos is advanced and dereferenced to read the link map presence byte without a default-link-map guard.
Initializes the output structure before parsing; part of the vulnerable function but not directly causing the out-of-bounds read.

Incomplete assignment (view truncated); in the full code this sets pos to the start of the element data, enabling subsequent dereferences that lead to the out-of-bounds read when the element uses a default link map.
Comment referencing a size validation function; indirectly related as the missing guard leads to reading beyond the element end.
